why: The student puts `else return -1` inside the loop as if 'otherwise' meant 'if it was not found anywhere', but in Java the method returns on the first pass, so only arr[0] is checked; the answer also finds no 'last' occurrence.

concepts.quote: if (arr[i] == key) return i; else return -1;
concepts.why: Exactly one branch runs on the first pass and both branches return, so -1 is returned before any later element is checked; 'otherwise' is read in its everyday sense of 'if never found'.
It uses arr[i] correctly to name the element at position i, but does nothing more with indexing.
It writes a valid comparison that gives a boolean (the int is promoted to double), with no further reasoning.
Both branches return, so the body runs at most once, yet the student expects the loop to search the whole array; the header is left out, so it does not go backwards to find the last occurrence.
